label: History
value: Anne was adopted by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: After being adopted by siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, Anne grew up at Green Gables in Avonlea, transforming her room in the east gable into a cozy sanctuary. At Avonlea School, she entered into a spirited academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe and joined Miss Stacy's special preparation class to study for the Entrance examination to Queen's Academy. During her time at Queen's Academy, Anne worked diligently, forming close friendships with students like Stella Maynard and Priscilla Grant while competing for top academic honors. Her hard work culminated in winning the Avery Scholarship. Following her studies, she taught at the Avonlea school for two years, actively participated in local community efforts such as the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and eventually prepared to leave for Redmond College alongside her companion Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye attended the Avonlea school.
unit: Anthony Pye attended the Avonlea school under the instruction of Anne Shirley. From the beginning, he held his new teacher in contempt and behaved with a scornful air of obedience, believing that female teachers were useless. He frequently disrupted the classroom, making negative remarks about Anne's hair and facial expressions, telling others that her hair was red and asserting that she always looked cross. While his behavior disturbed Anne, she attempted to win him over with patience and kindness. The turning point came when Anthony's persistent disobedience pushed Anne to administer a whipping; rather than harboring resentment, Anthony respected the firm discipline, declaring that the whipping was as good as a man's and conceding that Anne was worthwhile after all.

unit: Anthony Pye attended the Avonlea school under the instruction of Anne Shirley. From the beginning, he held his new teacher in contempt and behaved with a scornful air of obedience, believing that female teachers were useless. He frequently disrupted the classroom, making negative remarks about Anne's hair and facial expressions, telling others that her hair was red and asserting that she always looked cross. While his behavior disturbed Anne, she attempted to win him over with patience and kindness. The turning point came when Anthony's persistent disobedience pushed Anne to administer a whipping; rather than harboring resentment, Anthony respected the firm discipline, declaring that the whipping was as good as a man's and conceding that Anne was worthwhile after all.

label: Personality
value: Charlotta is a literal-minded handmaiden.
unit: Charlotta is a literal-minded, faithful, and energetic handmaiden who worries intensely over her mistress's well-being and household duties. Highly conscientious and lively, she flies around briskly when there is work to be done. She possesses a very practical, straightforward view of life, holding little patience for men or romantic idealizations while worrying about hypothetical misfortunes.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman came to live with Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge.
unit: Leonora Bowman came to live with Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge as a young girl, receiving board and care in exchange for her work. Miss Lavendar gave her the name 'Charlotta the Fourth' to avoid confusion with her three older sisters who had previously held the post before moving to Boston. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta served them biscuits and demonstrated the local echoes. She later confided in Anne about her deep concerns regarding Miss Lavendar's declining health and spirits, including an incident where she accidentally broke a cherished heirloom bowl without receiving any scolding. Upon learning that Stephen Irving was coming to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was overjoyed, secretly watching him from the kitchen window. Before Miss Lavendar's wedding, Charlotta worked tirelessly alongside Anne and Diana to prepare the home and food. On the wedding day, she dressed in her finest attire and watched the ceremony proceed smoothly.

Miss Lavendar gave her the name 'Charlotta the Fourth' to avoid confusion with her three older sisters who had previously held the post before moving to Boston. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta served them biscuits and demonstrated the local echoes. She later confided in Anne about her deep concerns regarding Miss Lavendar's declining health and spirits, including an incident where she accidentally broke a cherished heirloom bowl without receiving any scolding. Upon learning that Stephen Irving was coming to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was overjoyed, secretly watching him from the kitchen window. Before Miss Lavendar's wedding, Charlotta worked tirelessly alongside Anne and Diana to prepare the home and food. On the wedding day, she dressed in her finest attire and watched the ceremony proceed smoothly.

label: History
value: Davy's mother died in East Grafton.
unit: Following the death of his mother in East Grafton, Davy and his twin sister Dora were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert to live at Green Gables. During the drive to Avonlea, he exhibited his boundless energy, hugging Marilla and teasing his sister Dora. At Green Gables, he frequently tested Marilla's patience with his table manners, endless questions, and antics like climbing onto the pantry table and accidentally destroying lemon pies. He formed a strong emotional bond with Anne Shirley, who patiently guided his behavior, helped him understand moral lessons, and promised to dye feathers for his Indian headdress. Over time, his behavior improved as he began attending the local school. After the death of his uncle Richard Keith, who left a trust fund for the twins' upkeep, it was settled that Davy and Dora would reside permanently at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana met Anne Shirley in the Barry garden at Orchard Slope upon Anne's arrival in Avonlea.
unit: Upon Anne Shirley's arrival in Avonlea, Diana met her in the Barry garden at Orchard Slope, where the two girls instantly bonded and swore a solemn oath to be lifelong bosom friends. Diana shared in many childhood adventures, playhouses, and schoolroom experiences alongside Anne. During a sleepover at Orchard Slope, Diana and Anne entered a bed-racing contest without knowing her great-aunt Josephine Barry was sleeping in the spare room, causing severe outrage and nearly losing Diana her music lesson funding until Anne personally intervened. Soon after, Anne accidentally served Diana currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Diana to become intoxicated; as a result, Mrs. Barry temporarily forbade Diana from speaking to or playing with Anne until Anne saved Minnie May's life during an attack of croup. When Anne fractured her ankle after falling off the Barry house ridgepole on a dare, Diana frantically rushed to her aid and summoned her father for assistance. As she grew older, Diana joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving as its treasurer while continuing her close companionship with Anne.

During a sleepover at Orchard Slope, Diana and Anne entered a bed-racing contest without knowing her great-aunt Josephine Barry was sleeping in the spare room, causing severe outrage and nearly losing Diana her music lesson funding until Anne personally intervened. Soon after, Anne accidentally served Diana currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Diana to become intoxicated; as a result, Mrs. Barry temporarily forbade Diana from speaking to or playing with Anne until Anne saved Minnie May's life during an attack of croup. When Anne fractured her ankle after falling off the Barry house ridgepole on a dare, Diana frantically rushed to her aid and summoned her father for assistance. As she grew older, Diana joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving as its treasurer while continuing her close companionship with Anne.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert after their mother, Mary Keith, passes away. Upon moving to Green Gables, Dora behaves politely and ladylike, making a stark contrast to her unruly brother. She sleeps in Marilla's room and adjusts calmly to her new surroundings. In the autumn, Dora enters Avonlea School alongside Davy, where she is temporarily placed with older student Mirabel Cotton. After Mirabel tells her stories about deceased relatives and family ghosts, Dora becomes deeply frightened of the dark until Anne Shirley comforts her and settles her to sleep.

label: History
value: Gilbert lived in Alberta for three years
unit: After living in Alberta for three years with his father, Gilbert returned to Avonlea to resume his schooling. On his first afternoon back in the classroom, he pulled Anne Shirley's braid and called her 'Carrots', provoking her to smash her slate over his head. Though he later attempted to apologize, Anne refused to forgive him, initiating an intense academic rivalry between the two top scholars. label: History
value: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm
unit: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables and relocated to Avonlea from New Brunswick. He quickly developed a reputation among the locals as an eccentric crank due to his erratic meal schedules, unusual dishwashing habits, and outright refusal to subscribe to church funds or gossip with Mrs. Rachel Lynde. After a confrontation regarding Anne Shirley's stray cow, he unexpectedly formed a warm, friendly acquaintance with Anne when she came to confess to selling his Jersey cow by mistake. Though initially annoyed by his sailor brother's foul-mouthed parrot, Ginger, Mr. Harrison remains deeply attached to the bird despite the trouble it causes. He later expresses support for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, enjoying Anne's visits and lighthearted company.

label: History
value: Josie attended Avonlea School.
unit: Josie attended Avonlea School alongside Anne Shirley and her classmates. During a class spelling turn, Anne caught Josie peeping in her book to spell a word, causing Anne to flash her a look of scorn. On another occasion, Josie engaged in a game of daring in the Barry garden, successfully walking a board fence before daring Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof. After Anne accepted the dare and fell off the roof breaking her ankle, Josie later visited her during her recovery. She eventually prepared for and took the entrance examinations for Queen's Academy alongside her classmates, staying in town and pursuing her studies at the Academy.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived in an old stone house.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived in an old stone house built by her father eighty years prior. Twenty-five years ago, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but the engagement ended after a quarrel, after which Stephen left for the United States. Following the separation, Miss Lavendar dropped out of local social circles and lived an isolated life in Grafton, where she was served by her handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth. She spent much of her time indulging her imagination, inventing and playing games with a fictional dream-boy. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry unexpectedly stumbled upon her home while seeking directions to West Grafton and had tea with her. During their visit, Anne accidentally mentioned Stephen Irving's son, Paul, causing Miss Lavendar to inquire about him.

Following the separation, Miss Lavendar dropped out of local social circles and lived an isolated life in Grafton, where she was served by her handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth. She spent much of her time indulging her imagination, inventing and playing games with a fictional dream-boy. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry unexpectedly stumbled upon her home while seeking directions to West Grafton and had tea with her. During their visit, Anne accidentally mentioned Stephen Irving's son, Paul, causing Miss Lavendar to inquire about him.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert resides at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert resided at Green Gables with her unmarried brother Matthew, living a quiet and orderly life. Wanting help on the farm, they sent word to adopt an orphan boy, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley was sent instead. Although Marilla initially intended to return the young girl, she took pity on Anne after seeing Mrs. Blewett's severe nature and agreed to keep her. Over time, Marilla raised Anne with firm discipline and practical instruction, gradually growing deeply attached to her despite Anne's vivid imagination and frequent misadventures. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the loss of her brother and threats to her sight from failing health. To prevent Marilla from having to sell Green Gables, Anne gave up her university scholarship to stay home, cementing their lifelong maternal bond.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla, running their farm on the edge of Avonlea. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm work, Matthew traveled to Bright River station, only to find an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Anne Shirley waiting instead. Despite his severe shyness around women and girls, Matthew was captivated by Anne's lively chatter on the drive home and quickly favored keeping her at Green Gables. When Marilla considered giving Anne to the harsh Mrs. Blewett, Matthew firmly opposed the idea. Over time, Matthew quietly supported Anne, noticing details others missed; he even braved a store trip to buy her a dress with fashionable puffed sleeves for Christmas. After several years of quiet devotion to Anne and his farm, Matthew suffered fatal heart failure upon reading a newspaper report detailing the unexpected collapse of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Paul moved from Boston to Avonlea.
unit: Paul moved from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother on the shore road. At school, he became a devoted student of Anne Shirley, bonding deeply with her over shared imaginative thoughts, poetic fancies, and rock people creations. During his time in Avonlea, he engaged in a drawn physical fight with St. Clair Donnell after defending the Stars and Stripes flag, earning mutual respect for his patriotism. He also regularly writes letters and compositions to his teacher detailing his imaginary rock people like Nora, the Golden Lady, and the Twin Sailors. When his father, Stephen Irving, made an unexpected visit to Avonlea, Paul excitedly welcomed him and introduced him to Anne. Through Anne's connection with Miss Lavendar Lewis, Paul indirectly helps reconnect his father with his former romance.

unit: Mr. Phillips carries out his duties with a stern and sometimes high-handed discipline, resorting to public humiliation, corporal punishment, and assigning embarrassing seats. He exhibits clear favoritism toward his older scholars, spending significant class time giving special attention to Prissy Andrews under the guise of helping her with lessons. He also shows a lack of tact, openly labeling struggling students in front of the class.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at the Avonlea schoolhouse.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at the Avonlea schoolhouse, where he taught scholars across various grade levels. During class, he frequently focused his personal attention on Prissy Andrews by giving her individual assistance in algebra and Latin in the back of the room. When Gilbert Blythe teased Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her braid, Anne retaliated by breaking her slate over Gilbert's head; Mr. Phillips punished Anne by making her stand in front of the blackboard with a message written above her head. The following day, after Anne arrived late alongside several other pupils, Mr. Phillips singled her out for punishment by ordering her to sit with Gilbert Blythe, leading Anne to leave school and refuse to return under his instruction for a time. Despite his criticized teaching methods and stern discipline, driven students like Anne and Gilbert were able to advance to the fifth class under his curriculum and prepare for higher studies.

value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and childhood companion of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. She later attended Queen's Academy alongside her classmates and was recognized as the handsomest girl of her year. After completing her studies, she took a teaching position in Carmody. During this period, she received a marriage proposal from Nelson Atkins, which she rejected after discovering he had copied his words directly from an etiquette book.

label: History
value: Stacy was appointed as the schoolteacher
unit: Miss Stacy was appointed as the schoolteacher at Avonlea School. Recognizing potential in her students, she organized an advanced Queen's class to tutor them for an extra hour after school in preparation for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. During her time in Avonlea, she caught Anne Shirley reading a novel during class time, gently explaining the deceit involved and forgiving her. Though offered a job in her home district, Miss Stacy chose to stay in Avonlea to see her pupils through their studies. She led the class through their final year of preparation, gave them supportive advice prior to their entrance exams, and eventually concluded her rule as Avonlea's teacher at the end of the term in June.
